sections.description:
PROVINCIAL EMPLOYEES' SOCIAL SECURITY (PROCUREMENT OF SUPPLIES AND
PROPERTY) REGULATIONS, 1967
PROVINCIAL EMPLOYEES' SOCIAL SECURITY (PROCUREMENT OF SUPPLIES AND
PROPERTY) REGULATIONS, 1967
(Gaz. of West Pak. Pt. 1, 21 June 1968, p.
770, see 1968 LLC Statutes, 112.)
1. Title and commencement‑(1) These regulations may be called
the Provincial Employees' Social Security (Procurement of Supplies and
Property) Regulations, 1967.
(2) They shall come into force at
once.
2. Definitions:‑In these regulations, unless the context
otherwise requires‑
(i) the following expressions
shall have the meanings hereby respectively assigned to them, that is to say :‑
(a) "Ordinance" means
the Provincial Employees' Social Security Ordinance, 1965.
(b) "controlled
d6cuments" means documents which are serially numbered and for which
signatures are required when blank copies of the documents pass from one
officer to another ;
(ii) other expressions shall have
the meanings respectively assigned to them in Section 2 of the Ordinance.
3. Procurement of supplies. Subject to rules 7 and 9, in every case
where, in the opinion of the Commissioner, the cost of the supplies to be
purchased by the Institution is likely to amount to rupees two thousand or
over, purchase shall be by the method of public tender.
4. Purchasing Committee.‑A Purchasing Committee shall be
established by the Commissioner which shall consist of the Vice‑Commissioner
of the Institution as Chairman, the Head of the Finance and Accounts Department
of the Institution, and one other member to be nominated by the Commissioner in
relation to tire type of supplies to .be purchased. In the unavoidable absence
of any member the Commissioner shall appoint a representative to act in his
place:
(Proviso added by Noti. Lab. III‑II‑16/bb/66,
Gaz. of West Pak. Pt. I, 4 April 1959.)[Provided that the Commissioner may in his discretion appoint a
purchasing committee at each local office comprising of the Local Director
concerned or the officer incharge of the local Office, as the Chairman and such
other employees of the Institution, as he may deem necessary as members of the
Committee, and may delegate to such local purchasing committees all or any of
the powers of the purchasing committee at the Head Office. The local purchasing
committees shall in relation to the powers delegated to them, be governed by
the relevant previsions mutatis mutandis of these regulations.]
5. Duties of Purchasing Committee.‑Where provision for a
proposed purchase is included in the budget or the year as approved err deemed
tee have been approved by Government the Purchasing Committee shall‑‑‑
(1) insert, in at least two
newspapers which have wide circulation in West Pakistan‑
(a) an announcement of the
supplies to be purchased ;
(b) a general invitation to
suppliers to apply to the Institution for forma of tender ;
(c) a statement of the last date
for the receipt of tenders ;
(d) a statement of the time and
place of the meeting of the per. chasing Committee at which tenders shall be
opened which shall be after the data referred to at (iii) below ; and
(e) act invitation to invitation
to attend such meeting.
(ii) prepare the conditions of
tender, which shall include a provision that tenders shall be submitted on the
form or forms of tender refereed to at (i) (to) above and shall be stint to the
Institution in a sealed envelope marked prominently make the outside
"Tender No ---------------------------------- for
-------------------------------- last
date for receipt of tender:
(In its application to Sind, Regulations 5
(iii) subs. with the following ;.
(iii) Fix
the date by which tenders must be submitted, which shall not be less them seven
days (where the amount involved its purchases is upto Rs. 23.000 Ind not less
than 21 days (where the amount involved ice purchased exceeds Rs. 25.000, from
the date of announcement referred to at (i) (a) above."
